evidence:
Assigned row 35 only. Workbook Quality Checks D36 requires defining behavior plus reload/re-auth and server-backed durability; Internal Quality Checks D36 agrees. The frozen template requires a real restart (functional/judge.toml:39-46), and current REVIEW_POLICY distinguishes fresh-context storage evidence from a same-context reload.

PUBLIC BEHAVIOR -> GRADED OBSERVATION: instruction.md:1-3 defines a saved all-or-none coordinated compensation change, stale-history refusal and original receipt replay after later changes/restart. hireops_rules.md:437-440 requires durable non-reserving previews; :443-478 requires complete-set netting, atomic member effects, durable immutable batch receipt and restart replay. functional/judge.toml:911 explicitly grades the fully-funded two-requisition cycle and 60/40 -> 80/20 offset; :920 grades persisted source/successor lineage; :965 requires saved preview fresh signed-in readback without economic mutation; :992 and :1001 test stale-member and ABA refusal against actual successful controls; :1028/:1037/:1046 grade identical retries, conflicting distinct operations and disjoint operations. These are defining behavior, not a static screen or response-shape substitute.

SERVER-BACKING / DURABILITY: constraints/judge.toml:23-25 creates a unique requisition plus new pending offer through the UI and retrieves their saved identities, association and entered values in a new independent empty signed-in browser context; it explicitly excludes no-op/static/browser-only mutation. functional/prompt.md:9 and :15 require newContext with separate cookies/storage, forbid treating a same-context reload as shared storage, and permit an equivalent supported separate-context tool. Functional P10 (:49) records successful ordinary records, lineage/financial/audit facts, saved B previews and original committed receipt before the one restart. hro_restart (judge.toml:902) compares those recorded values after restart and re-auth and checks no reseeding overwrite/duplicates; hro_change_retry_restart (:1073) separately replays the original committed operation with unchanged receipt and no extra effects. The functional MCP wiring (:14-18) supplies the same restart helper contract as the frozen template. UI-observed routes, generated IDs, equivalent money/date presentations and layouts are allowed (prompt.md:13,53; app_context.md:25-27), without requiring same-origin assets or reading source to infer SQLite.

ACTUAL LOCAL OBSERVATIONS: batch-domain/results.json records successful fully-funded netting, immutable original receipt replay after later revision/rescission, and restart-preserved financial state/drafts/receipt. The driver shows actual stop/start and reauthentication at batch-domain.cjs:117-119, then deep equality of financial state, saved change sets and the original commit result; this is an HTTP product probe, not the configured judge or the shared MCP restart. batch-ui.cjs:29-34 drives ordinary preview/commit; :44-53 forwards a real successful commit but drops its browser response, retries the same saved operation and compares effects; :54 opens an independent Auditor context and retrieves the committed operation. Its five results are successful. install-lifecycle.py:38-47 invokes the actual shared restart MCP, checks replacement PID and old-process exit, signs in again and compares the saved requisition; results show PID 21 -> 97 and a successful restart response. MCP results separately show the real browser tool can create a new context, sign in independently and retrieve the newly saved requisition. gate-witness results show the no-op-create variant does not satisfy the storage gate, while dead approval passes only that deliberately narrow prerequisite and remains exposed to functional core checks.

HASH VERIFICATION: current raw-index input_sha256 equals this assigned input. SHA256s were recomputed and match its entries: batch-domain.cjs 80eb13e01fc5d9bb9514bec35721a8c0619dd1eda75c6ed6a48be8c5858a2f0d; batch-domain/results.json 0c7f4da8fdc1037091fda6b28f5f2211f0ab1dfef0e1d7f2fb03c53c617d8af1; batch-ui.cjs 899a7309c67b2ca5f951ced6ce65c8e8c63634f5e892cc0427b4d97fef109821; batch-ui/results.json c58daecb432c2bde6e4b005c42e85662c3a7b4810f1aa828f6ba69708656a6e5; install-lifecycle.py 05780ac5eb6f1e441ef5a946a36f466ad7cdee7ae239b5f7d7d9f5933f39e024; install-lifecycle/results.json 368261834b06931f2e8ac0fa0fd909a435e7ae28a6c30444c3ff48240d27bb24; gate-witness.cjs 08ee689584d24a97a8446fb32ca0c4f9d3df100bd6eec14560c4fa63ad8ae31c; gate-witness/results.json fd8410bc91102874ef98edfdbacf19f7853687956e076acc684d36c565d9ec75; mcp/results.json bad8d80ee96bda6a46775d4dfcc508371b96c50e3106cd9f4e27ffee1a6e4cc3. All 13 install-lifecycle solution-app hashes, all 14 batch-UI solution hashes and all four batch-domain domain-source hashes match the frozen task bytes.

ADVERSARIAL REASONING: a browser-local finance desk that keeps only seed responses on its server cannot satisfy the unique empty-context intake readback; an in-memory server that shares records between browsers but loses them on process exit fails P10; a sequential transfer implementation rejects the fully-funded cycle and fails hro_change_net_budget; a receipt recomputed from current successors fails later and restart replay. A conforming alternative using generated IDs, different routes and an initially empty operational desk remains exercisable because controls are newly created and discovered by UI. No assigned-row false-pass or false-fail was established.

LIMIT: these inspected local runs establish bounded product/tool observations and row-35 coverage, not execution of the complete configured LLM rubric, full judge duration, Oracle/model score or portal acceptance. The raw index explicitly lacks those measurements. This row does not waive the separate runtime-evidence requirements owned by the relevant quality rows.
